answer: Poisson-duty fingerprinting: each agent must emit a 24h keepalive train whose inter-arrival histogram and burst-size spectrum follow a per-agent sinusoidal schedule, routed through an isolated egress haven and tagged with an umber-coded watermark. Aggregators correlate cross-identity timing. An attacker can forge many IDs, but must provide independent wake schedules, sockets, and egress with low timing covariance; shared runtimes leave detectable correlations. Cost is sustained parallel traffic and infrastructure, not registration.
